invariants.statement: Every protected datum has exactly one dataClass, owner, representation, key/HMAC class and audit/access coverage; no unregistered sensitive field exists.
Encryption and HMAC keys are strictly separated; no key crosses purpose; cross-purpose decrypt or lookup must fail.
Envelope shape, key_ref parsing and AEAD/AAD are fixed; unknown/malformed/retired key_ref, wrong purpose or decryption failure must fail closed with no plaintext fallback.
HMAC is lowercase 64-hex under an independent key; it is used only for equality, uniqueness and indexed lookup and is never returned, logged or public.
Every key and credential has an owner, custody, state, rotation and recovery path; secret material never enters a database, code, image or log.
Rotation never rewrites append-only or frozen rows; historical keys are retained until retention; A2 replay returns the same payload/decision without re-selection or a second reservation.
The five authentication domains never share a token, credential, audience or verifier; a request that crosses domains is rejected.
The six service identities use least privilege, independent CAM roles and rotation; no frontend holds a service secret and no policy grants a wildcard action or resource.
Every IVR request must pass mTLS, signature, timestamp and nonce verification; the verification order and canonical string are fixed.
Replay rejection occurs before any domain side effect; transport nonce and timestamp are refreshed on every retry while A2 eventId and payload stay unchanged.
Provider callbacks require mTLS, vendor signature, timestamp and nonce; the same event and fingerprint is idempotent while a changed payload is a conflict.
